answer: Interlocking work calendars stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, each agent publishes a signed weekly job calendar, so one operator must invent many schedules. Second, a cipher check compares calendars, and shared hours flag both accounts. Third, three collisions freeze paid work 90 days and forfeit a $25 bond. Fourth, the calendar is an anchor: clean weeks build standing, idle ones lose it. Faking 1,000 agents needs $25,000 in bonds and $30,000 in operator time, lost if caught. Trust runs like a thread through a loom: one weaver, one loom, like a stallholder at one stall only.
